frozen_before_hardware_access: v1 frozen before hardware access; amendment 1 (2026-08-24) appends B300-only candidates after the first capacity measurement -- see amendments

profiles.B300: 288 GB HBM3e — conditional deep-batch stages 8-10 exist for this capacity and remain subject to the extension rule
profiles.B200: 180 GB HBM3e — the original stage list; conditional stages may still run if the extension rule holds

measurements_per_stage: peak and reserved HBM; steady-state free-HBM fraction
throughput stability (decode tokens/s spread across four wall-clock windows of each stream's steady state; see B200_BACKEND_SELECTION_POLICY amendment 1)
startup, model load, finalize, resume overhead
extension_rule: Conditional stages (8+) and any additional worker counts (12, 16) or batch sizes (64) may be tested ONLY if every prior stage completed without OOM or integrity failure AND the predeclared cost rule holds: projected additional benchmark time <= 25% of remaining authorized runtime after reserving the affordability-gate calibration budget. No open-ended search.
stop_rules: stop immediately on any OOM (larger configurations are not attempted)
stop immediately on any integrity failure
stop launching new stages at 95% budget consumption (watchdog)
each stage runs the full validation corpus exactly once; no cherry-picking
a non-reference stage that fails (OOM, integrity, structural) is INELIGIBLE, never a session abort: REFERENCE_SERIAL is the terminal fallback
selection: policies/B200_BACKEND_SELECTION_POLICY.json — highest verified rows/hour among gate-eligible candidates; extra B300 capacity is exploited ONLY through these mechanically measured stages, never through scientific redesign
note: v2 of the order frozen during the B300 migration, before any provider instance was rented. Stages 1-7 are byte-identical to the v1 order validated for the B200; stages 8-10 are the capacity-conditional deep-batch extension for the 288 GB part. It must not be reordered on the accelerator.

amendments.rule: PRE-CALIBRATION BUDGET: the non-O1 equivalence phase and the benchmark together may use at most 25% of the authorized runtime remaining when the phase starts. The reference stage always runs (it is the terminal fallback and the equivalence anchor). Other stages run in the frozen order, each only if its projected cost (the largest stage time measured so far, initially the reference pass) fits the remaining budget; a stage that does not fit is skipped and therefore ineligible. The result of the whole phase is mirrored durably and restored on a replacement pod whose image digest, profile and benchmark order match, so an eviction never repays the phase.
amendments.why: the phase ran 21 full-corpus passes (~55% of the calibration workload) before the affordability gate, was unbounded, and was repeated in full after every eviction against a shrinking allocation
amendments.scientific_impact: none: selection input only; every stage that runs still runs the full corpus exactly once

amendments.field: staged_candidates (append only; stages 11-13, B300 profile only)
amendments.was: the deepest candidate was stage 10, B200_BATCHED_w1_b48; the extension_rule pre-authorised testing batch size 64 but the candidate list did not contain it, and nothing beyond 64 was listed
amendments.why:
The order was frozen before ANY hardware access and was sized for the B200's 180 GB. B300 (288 GB) was added later as a profile, and this file already marks stages 8-10 'conditional' for exactly that reason. First hardware access on 2026-08-24 (reports/B300_HARDWARE_EVIDENCE.json) measured b48 using 12.1 GB of 287.4 GB -- 4% of the device. The frozen list therefore does not span the capacity of the profile it is being run on. Concretely, the full combined session's generation work (4,608 O1 rows + 8,910 FL episode-walks = 13,518 row-equivalents) does not fit the USD 40 compute allocation at b48.

This amendment adds CANDIDATES ONLY. It does not select anything and it does not touch the selection rule, which remains mechanical: highest verified completed rows/hour AMONG ELIGIBLE configurations. A config becomes eligible only by passing its own structural-equivalence gates against REFERENCE_SERIAL (row IDs, task hashes, prompt tokens, action mapping, axis/sign/alpha mapping, stream and seed mapping, record schema, canonical ordering). If b64/b128/b256 diverge on any of those they are INELIGIBLE regardless of throughput, exactly as before, and the existing fallback chain stands.

The justification is the capacity measurement, NOT the throughput measurement. Selecting a configuration because it was observed to be fast is prohibited by this policy and that prohibition is unchanged; what is corrected here is that the candidate list did not cover the hardware.
amendments.bounded_by: unchanged: the existing extension_rule cost bound (additional benchmark time <= 25% of remaining authorized runtime after reserving the calibration budget) and the existing stop_rules (stop on first OOM, larger configurations not attempted; stop on any integrity failure). No open-ended search: the list ends at 256, the deepest batch measured at FULL 256-token row length.
amendments.scientific_impact: none by construction: candidate list only. Every added configuration must earn eligibility through the same unmodified equivalence gates, and REFERENCE_SERIAL remains the terminal fallback.

amendments.field: PRECALIBRATION_BUDGET_FRACTION, and the per-stage cost estimate used by the pre-calibration cost rule
amendments.was: Amendment 2 bounded the equivalence phase and the benchmark TOGETHER to 25% of the authorized runtime remaining when the phase starts, while also requiring that the reference stage always runs. On real hardware those two clauses cannot both hold: the reference pass is ~37% of the session (~1.9 h of ~5.1 h over the 384-row corpus), so the implemented expression 0.25 * remaining - t_reference is negative and clamps to zero. Separately, and independently fatal, each stage's cost was estimated as max(t_reference, largest stage measured so far): every non-reference stage was estimated at the cost of REFERENCE_SERIAL, the SLOWEST configuration that exists, so the cheapest deep-batch stages were always the first to be skipped and could never be reached however much budget remained.
amendments.now: The fraction bounds only the DISCRETIONARY stages, computed on the runtime remaining AFTER the mandatory reference pass: budget = 0.50 * max(0, remaining - t_reference). A fraction cannot bound mandatory work, because the reference always runs. Each stage's cost is estimated per configuration as t_reference / (workers * batch) plus a fixed overhead, corrected upward by the worst under-estimate observed so far, which is the model the benchmark phase already used. Both phases now share one estimator; their disagreement was the defect.
amendments.why: Measured on real B300 hardware 2026-08-24 (reports/B300_HARDWARE_EVIDENCE.json). Under the previous rule NO non-reference stage runs at any budget: every batched configuration is recorded 'eligible_structurally: false, skipped: precalibration cost rule' WITHOUT EVER BEING TESTED. With the shared estimator, at the current reference extrapolation, 10 of the 12 non-reference stages are tested (B200_REPLICA_w2_b1 and B200_BATCHED_w1_b4 are still skipped untested) and b256 is among those tested.
amendments.bounded_by: The reference pass is paid once (shared with the benchmark rather than repeated). The halving rule reserves half of the REMAINING budget per accepted stage, which is not the same as bounding the phase to half the budget: because stage costs fall geometrically down the frozen order while the threshold only halves per acceptance, the equivalence phase converges to ~84% of the shared budget at the nominal reference, leaving the benchmark phase ~16%. A stage that does not fit is still skipped, still recorded, and still ineligible, so the phase fails closed; but the 50/50 split this fraction appears to promise is NOT delivered, and a configuration that passes equivalence but is never benchmarked cannot be selected.
not_amended: structural equivalence gates (row IDs, task hashes, prompt tokens, action mapping, axis/sign/alpha mapping, stream/seed mapping, record schema, canonical ordering)
the frozen stage order and the identity of stages 1-10
the rule that the reference stage always runs and is the terminal fallback
amendments.scientific_impact: None to the science. This changes only which configurations get the CHANCE to earn an equivalence verdict, and every stage that runs still runs the full corpus exactly once and must still pass every gate unchanged. A configuration without its own equivalence verdict remains ineligible, even when it is the fastest.
amendments.robustness: NOT robust to a slower reference pass, and not monotone. Replaying the rule against the real estimator at multiples of the extrapolated reference: 1.0x -> 10/12 stages, b256 tested; 1.5x -> 7/12, tested; 2.0x -> 5/12, b256 NOT tested; 2.15x -> 4/12, tested; 2.7x -> 0/12. An earlier draft of this amendment claimed the result 'remains true even if the reference pass proves 2.15x slower'; that was a single lucky sample point, not a property, and it is withdrawn. The reference pass duration is not yet measured on hardware.
amendments.does_not_affect_calibration_cost: IMPORTANT, and contrary to an earlier draft of this amendment: selecting a batched backend does NOT make the calibration cheaper. The sealed v2.1 orchestrator constructs RealBackend directly (o1_packages/O1_oracle_reachability_v2.1.0_source/o1_v210/run_o1_v2_orchestrator.py:505,674), exposes no backend/worker/batch CLI argument, and calls generate() one task at a time. The calibration therefore runs at the REFERENCE_SERIAL rate whichever configuration this policy selects; affordability() projects from the serial rate for exactly this reason. The selected backend governs the non-O1 benchmark and the precommit record only. The withdrawn claim that this buys a '~50x cheaper' calibration was false.
